name: Ruins of Zul'Mamwe
summary: Skullsplitter warriors hold the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe in central Stranglethorn Vale, south of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. Cliffs ring the ancient stone platforms on nearly every side, and Ana'thek the Cruel rules the stronghold.

sections.title: Stronghold of the Skullsplitters
sections.body: In central Stranglethorn Vale, the Skullsplitters hold the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe as one of their chief seats of power. Mountains form a natural amphitheater around the site, open only to the north. From weathered ziggurats and stone terraces, Chief Ana'thek the Cruel directs his warriors and witch doctors. They defend their ground fiercely against intruders and rival jungle troll tribes.

sections.title: Remnants of an Ancient Empire
sections.body: Zul'Mamwe's stones come from the ancient Gurubashi Empire, which once ruled the southern reaches of the continent without rival. The empire broke apart long ago into hostile factions. Among the overgrown masonry and broken monoliths, the Skullsplitters guard these ancestral stones and keep their age-old tribal rituals.

faq.q: Who controls the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe?
faq.answer: The Skullsplitter troll tribe holds the ruins, one of Stranglethorn Vale's two dominant and aggressive jungle troll tribes. Their chieftain, Ana'thek the Cruel, commands them there.
Zul'Mamwe lies in central Stranglethorn Vale, just south of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. Mountains ring the encampment on nearly every side, with a valley pass to the north as its main approach.

faq.q: Why are the Skullsplitters hostile to travelers?
faq.answer: The Skullsplitters are fiercely isolationist and hostile to outsiders. They see all other races and rival troll tribes as trespassers on their ancestral lands, and Ana'thek the Cruel leads them against anyone who approaches their jungle sanctuary.

faq.q: What is the history behind these ruins?
faq.answer: Zul'Mamwe's stone structures date to the height of the Gurubashi Empire. After the empire collapsed into warring splinter factions, the Skullsplitters claimed the site as an inland base of operations and kept its ancient stone terraces.

angles.text: As a Darkspear troll of the Horde, you may see Zul'Mamwe as a reminder of jungle kin who clung to savage, insular ways. They kept bloodthirsty traditions and refused to adapt to the wider world.
